title: Tenant RBAC seed operator and credential-rotation Helm hooks
author: Aisha Rahman
description:
Motivation:
Private installer upgrades and bootstraps historically required ad-hoc scripts and manual kubeadmin steps to populate tenant-scoped RBAC. That approach causes outages during rolling upgrades, leaves stale bootstrap tokens, and complicates safe rollback. This PR introduces an idempotent Tenant RBAC Seed Operator, Terraform outputs to wire tenant service identities, and Helm pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks that run a credential rotation + validation flow.

What this change does (summary):
- Add a lightweight 'tenant-rbac-seed-operator' component (controller + reconciler) that guarantees tenant Roles, RoleBindings, and namespace-scoped service accounts are present and reconciled from a compact policy bundle (policies/tenants/*). The operator is designed to be idempotent and safe to run during upgrades.
- Introduce a new CLI helper (installer bin: rbin rbac-rotate) invoked by Helm hooks that performs ephemeral bootstrap token rotation and a preflight RBAC smoke test against the target tenant namespace. The hook implements exponential backoff and emits structured JSON diagnostics for the console.
- Terraform module (modules/tenant-bootstrap) now exposes outputs: tenant_bootstrap_sa, tenant_bootstrap_role_arn, and bootstrap_secret_id to allow infra automation to provision short-lived credentials in cloud KMS/secret stores.
- Helm chart changes: add templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-job.yaml and templates/hooks/post-upgrade-job.yaml. Pre-upgrade validates existing bindings and rotates the bootstrap token; post-upgrade runs a verification job and triggers the operator reconciliation if any mismatches are detected.
- Add a rollback playbook (deploy/rollback/tenant-rbac-rollback.md) describing how the operator can be used to undo namespace-level RoleBinding changes and how to revoke bootstrap credentials via the new CLI.

Why this approach: 
- Operator-based reconciliation removes a class of timing-related upgrade failures when Helm attempts to apply RBAC changes before CRDs/namespaces are ready.
- Hooked credential rotation prevents a long-lived bootstrap secret from being relied upon across upgrades and reduces blast radius if a secret is leaked.
- Terraform outputs make the bootstrap flow auditable and usable by infra-as-code (cloud-init, onboarding scripts).

Testing & QA: 
- Unit tests for the operator reconciler and the hook job runner (go test ./cmd/... and controller tests using envtest) included.
- E2E in perf-canary lab: created a clustered scenario with 10 tenants and ran 3 upgrade iterations validating zero downtime for inference-serving route (latency SLOs preserved).
- Added integration tests for the rbac-rotate CLI verifying rotation, secret write to a mocked KMS, and verification of resolved RoleBindings.

Migration notes: 
- The operator adds a new CRD: TenantRBACSeed — it is optional for existing installs. If the CRD is not installed, Helm falls back to running the hook jobs (legacy behavior).
- Operators are enabled by default in new private deployments. Existing private installs can opt in via values.privateInstaller.enableTenantOperator=false.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature branch -> staging rollout with operator enabled; Helm pre/post hooks will run automatically.
2) Observe for two upgrade windows and monitor rbac.seed.operator metrics (rbac_seed_reconciles_total, rbac_seed_errors_total).
3) Gradually enable for select customers before wide rollout.

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/rbin/rbac-rotate/main.go (CLI entrypoint + rotation logic)
- operator/tenant-seed-controller/* (reconciler, manifest generator, controller registration)
- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-job.yaml
- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/post-upgrade-job.yaml
- terraform/modules/tenant-bootstrap/outputs.tf (exports for service account and secret)
- policies/tenants/* (compact YAML policy bundles)
- deploy/rollback/tenant-rbac-rollback.md

Backward compatibility and safety: 
- All changes are additive; no existing CRs are mutated without explicit opt-in.
- Helm hooks include timeouts and will not block indefinite upgrades; hooks can be skipped with --set privateInstaller.hooks.skip=true for emergency operations.

Follow-ups (separate PRs planned):
- Add monitoring dashboards for credential rotation frequency and hook latency.
- Add RBAC migration tool that will generate a diff/plan and allow staged RoleBinding migrations across tenants.

References: 
- Linear: ENG-2321 (tenant rbac automation), ENG-2388 (installer hooks), PM-4112 (private GA requirements)
- Internal runbook: infra/ops/tenant-bootstrap.md

release_notes: Add tenant RBAC seed operator, Helm pre/post upgrade hooks for credential rotation, Terraform outputs for tenant bootstrap; optional operator for private installations to ensure safe RBAC bootstrapping and rotation.
testing_instructions:
1) helm upgrade --install charts/private-installer --set privateInstaller.enableTenantOperator=true --namespace redwood-system
2) kubectl -n redwood-system logs job/pre-upgrade-rbac-rotate -f to observe rotation flow
3) verify secret rotation by checking terraform outputs consumer or reading mocked KMS in tests
4) run e2e fixture: go test ./e2e -run TestTenantRBACUpgrade
5) to rollback: follow deploy/rollback/tenant-rbac-rollback.md steps
notes_for_ops:
- Monitor metrics: rbac_seed_reconciles_total, rbac_seed_errors_total, rbac_rotate_job_duration_seconds
- If hooks are blocking, set privateInstaller.hooks.skip=true and run rbin rbac-rotate manually with --dry-run to inspect differences
- Emergency revoke: rbin rbac-rotate --revoke --tenant TENANT_ID
